source_title: Oxford Instruments plc Report and Financial Statements 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 114 and 155 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 11 June 2019; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 12.4%, adjusted operating profit 6.9%, adjusted profit before tax 12.3% and cash generated from operations increased substantially. Reported margin fell 80 basis points, mainly from currency and deliberate operational-excellence investment; cash conversion was 103%, net debt became net cash and the dividend increased.
already_announced_exclusion: The Horizon operational-excellence reshaping and operating-practice changes already implemented or disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The modest margin decline is specifically explained by currency and planned investment and is overwhelmed by strong orders, revenue, profit, cash conversion and balance-sheet improvement.

source_title: Oxford Instruments plc Report and Financial Statements 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 136 and 177 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 7 June 2021; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: COVID-19 constrained customer access, manufacturing capacity, shipments and selected end markets, leaving revenue broadly flat. Even so orders rose 5.3%, adjusted operating profit 12.3%, margin 190 basis points and net cash to £97.6m; cash conversion remained 101% and the order book grew 13.2%.
already_announced_exclusion: The Horizon efficiency measures, hybrid-working changes and accelerated service transformation already implemented before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Pandemic disruption was broad but temporary and did not translate into financial deterioration: profit, margin, orders, cash and the balance sheet all strengthened materially.

source_title: Oxford Instruments plc Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 97 and 115 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors on 14 July 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Supply-chain disruption, export-licence refusals and inflation affected delivery and one segment, but Group orders rose 20.9%, revenue 21.1%, adjusted operating profit 21.4% and statutory profit before tax 54.4%. Margin held at 18.1%, net cash rose to £100.2m, cash conversion was 88% and liquidity headroom remained substantial.
already_announced_exclusion: The withdrawal from complex bespoke cryogenic systems, associated resource redirection and the WITec integration disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Operational constraints were explicit but the Group converted them into strong order, revenue, profit and cash growth while preserving margin and substantial liquidity.
